verdict.summary: You can create a Local External Client App (ECA) in your own org and connect within the hour, with no review. Since Spring '26, new Connected Apps are blocked, so this has to be an ECA. To reach users in other Salesforce orgs you need a Packaged ECA inside a managed package, and each customer org's admin has to install it. AppExchange (now AgentExchange) security review, roughly 4-6+ weeks, is only documented as a requirement for a marketplace listing.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for your own org; several days for a managed package; weeks of prep work if you list on AppExchange
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 15-45 min (an ECA can take up to 30 min to start working)
verdict.approval_wait: none for your own org or direct package installs; about 4-6 weeks officially (6-9 weeks reported) for an AppExchange listing

gates.name: Local External Client App (your org)
gates.unlocks: You (an admin) can connect your own Salesforce org through your own OAuth client in Composio.
limits: New ECAs can take up to 30 minutes to become operational
Local ECAs are not copied when a sandbox is cloned or refreshed
Developer Edition API allowance is reported at 15,000 requests per rolling 24 hours (community source)
System Administrators automatically have Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps, which bypasses the uninstalled-app block

gates.name: Pre-authorized / installed users in your org
gates.unlocks: Other users in the same org can authorize the app once it is installed or they are pre-authorized through profiles or permission sets.
limits: New users cannot use an uninstalled app: they get 'app must be installed into org' / OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC
Users who authorized before the block keep access, except on device-flow apps, which are blocked for everyone
Installing requires Customize Application plus Modify All Data or Manage Connected Apps
No documented user count cap for unreviewed apps

gates.name: Packaged ECA in a managed package (other orgs); optional AppExchange/AgentExchange listing
gates.unlocks: Users in any customer org whose admin installs your managed package. An AppExchange listing makes the app discoverable in the marketplace.
limits: Only Packaged ECAs can be deployed to other orgs (2GP or 1GP managed packages)
Each customer org's admin must install the app, or new users there are blocked

AppExchange listing requires the security review, partner program enrollment, a $2,700 fee per paid app (free apps pay nothing) and $150/yr listing fee per Salesforce's page ($999 per a third-party source)
Periodic re-reviews every 6 months to 2 years
gates.time_to_reach: Days for packaging and installs; about 4-6 weeks review from a complete submission for a listing (6-9 weeks reported, 5-9 months to a live listing)

steps.title: Get admin access to a Salesforce org
steps.detail: Use an org where you are a System Administrator, or have Customize Application plus Modify All Data or Manage Connected Apps. You need these permissions to create and install the app.
gotchas: It has not been confirmed that a free Developer Edition org can still create ECAs after Spring '26 (see open questions).

steps.title: Create a new External Client App (not a Connected App)
steps.detail: In Setup, go to App Manager and click New External Client App. Set Distribution State to Local if only your org will use it, or Packaged if you plan to distribute it to other orgs. Then enable OAuth.
gotchas: Since Spring '26, new Connected Apps cannot be created in the UI or through the Metadata API. Only Salesforce Support can re-enable creation, and future releases will remove that option.
Local ECAs are not copied into cloned or refreshed sandboxes.

steps.title: Set the Callback URL
steps.detail: In the ECA's OAuth settings, paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into Callback URL. Salesforce rejects any redirect_uri that doesn't exactly match one of the entries.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The URL must be HTTPS or a custom URI scheme.
Put multiple callbacks on separate lines. The field holds at most 2000 characters.

steps.title: Select OAuth scopes that cover what Composio requests
steps.detail: Composio requests full, refresh_token and openid by default. Every scope the client requests must also be enabled on the app, so select Full access (full), Perform requests at any time (refresh_token, offline_access) and Allow access to your unique identifier (openid). Add api and web if you will narrow Composio's scopes to them.
gotchas: If Composio requests a scope that isn't selected on the ECA, authorization fails.

steps.title: Review flow and token policies
steps.detail: Keep the Authorization Code (web server) flow. Enable JWT Bearer Flow and upload a certificate only if you need server-to-server JWT. Decide on refresh token rotation and refresh token expiry: Salesforce's CLI guide uses 90 days at most for refresh tokens and a 15-minute session timeout.
gotchas: With rotation on, each refresh token works only once, and reusing an old one invalidates the current token.
A third-party source reports that refresh tokens unused for 30 days expire on production orgs from 4 Nov 2026.

steps.title: Copy Consumer Key and Secret into a custom Composio auth config
steps.detail: From the ECA's settings, copy the Consumer Key and Consumer Secret into a Composio Salesforce auth config that uses your own credentials. Keep the login.salesforce.com authorize and token URLs.

steps.title: Wait for the ECA to activate, then run a test authorization
steps.detail: Wait up to 30 minutes after creating the ECA, then start a Composio connection and sign in with your own Salesforce user. An 'invalid_client_id' error usually means the app hasn't propagated yet or the key is wrong.
gotchas: A redirect_uri that is mismatched or not URL-encoded makes the approval fail.

steps.title: Pre-authorize or install for other users in your org
steps.detail: Set Permitted Users to 'Admin approved users are pre-authorized', which Salesforce recommends, and assign the profiles or permission sets that should have access. Then confirm the app shows as installed on the Connected Apps OAuth Usage page; if it shows an Install button, click it.
gotchas: Uninstalled apps block new users with 'app must be installed into org'.
Give the Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps permission only to highly trusted users such as admins and testers.

steps.title: Package the ECA for other orgs
steps.detail: To serve users in other orgs, use a Packaged ECA and ship it in a 2GP (or 1GP) managed package. Each customer org's admin installs the package, which is also what lifts the uninstalled-app block in their org.
gotchas: If you already ship a Connected App inside a managed package, you are responsible for releasing a migrated ECA version for your customers.

steps.title: Prepare for AppExchange/AgentExchange security review (listing only)
steps.detail: Only needed if you want a marketplace listing. Complete the two required Trailhead modules, confirm enrollment and a contract in the AppExchange Partner Program, and run Checkmarx plus a web scanner (ZAP) through the Partner Security Portal. If your app calls third-party endpoints you don't own, get the third party's written consent for Salesforce to test them.
gotchas: The official page carries a 2017 footer and mentions Chimera, which third parties report was retired, so parts of it may be stale.

steps.title: Draft security review documentation
steps.detail: An agent can draft the architecture and data-flow documentation and collect scan reports. Incomplete documentation and an unready test environment are the most commonly cited causes of delay.

steps.title: Submit and wait for review
steps.detail: Salesforce quotes about 4-6 weeks from a complete submission; third parties report 6-9 weeks once queue time and fixes are counted. Later versions of an approved managed package are auto-approved, and periodic re-reviews follow every 6 months to 2 years.
gotchas: The fee for paid apps is $2,700 per Salesforce's page and $999 per attempt per a third-party source. Confirm with your Partner Account Manager.

steps.title: Plan for upcoming OAuth flow retirements
steps.detail: Third-party summaries report that the device flow is limited to local ECAs with a localhost callback from 30 Nov 2026, and that the username-password and user-agent flows retire on 20 Feb 2027. Use the authorization code flow, or JWT bearer / client credentials for headless jobs, and make sure the integration uses its refresh token at least monthly.

blockers.symptom: There's no option to create a new Connected App, or creation through the Metadata API fails
blockers.cause: Since Spring '26, Salesforce has disabled creating new Connected Apps.
blockers.fix: Create an External Client App instead. Only Salesforce Support can re-enable Connected App creation, and only temporarily.

blockers.symptom: error=invalid_client, 'app must be installed into org', OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC or OAUTH_APP_BLOCKED
blockers.cause: The app isn't installed in the user's org, and the user lacks Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps.
blockers.fix: Have an admin install the app from the Connected Apps OAuth Usage page (or install your managed package), or pre-authorize users through profiles or permission sets.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails with a redirect_uri mismatch
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri doesn't exactly match a Callback URL entry, or isn't URL-encoded.
blockers.fix: Copy the exact Composio callback URL into the ECA's Callback URL field.

blockers.cause: Composio requested a scope that isn't enabled on the ECA.
blockers.fix: Enable full, refresh_token and openid on the ECA, or reduce the scopes in Composio.

blockers.symptom: invalid_client_id right after you create the app
blockers.cause: An ECA can take up to 30 minutes to become operational.
Reported restriction of the device flow from 30 Nov 2026.
blockers.fix: Switch to a local ECA with a localhost callback, or move to JWT bearer or client credentials.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed OAuth app: it uses login.salesforce.com with the full, refresh_token and openid scopes. Bring your own app only if you need your own app identity, a packaged app for customer orgs, or control over the redirect URI. Your own app must be an External Client App, because new Connected Apps can't be created since Spring '26, and it must enable at least the scopes Composio requests.

open_questions: Exact Composio redirect URI: the toolkit lists https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but a v3 callback was also seen. Use the URL shown in your Composio auth config.
Can a free Developer Edition org still create new ECAs under the Spring '26 restrictions? Not verified in a live org.
Does a Packaged ECA distributed in a managed package outside AppExchange require any Salesforce review? The findings only document review for AppExchange/AgentExchange listings.
Can a Local ECA authorize users from other orgs through login.salesforce.com? The findings only say Packaged ECAs can be deployed to other orgs.
Security review fee conflict: $2,700 (Salesforce page with a 2017 footer) vs $999 (third party). Confirm with a Partner Account Manager.
Parts of the security review page may be stale; it still references Chimera, which third parties report was retired.
The refresh-token idle expiry (4 Nov 2026) and device-flow cutoff (30 Nov 2026) come from third-party summaries. Check Salesforce's release-update pages directly.
Does refresh token rotation work with Composio's token refresh handling? Not verified.
Field-by-field ECA settings were cited from search snippets, not full page fetches, so console labels may differ slightly.
